system.name: STRAW
system.one_liner: a wordline-level read-reclaim technique for NAND flash that tracks accumulated read-disturbance per wordline and reclaims only heavily-disturbed ones

content.key_idea: STRAW tracks a read counter per block and per wordline; every interval it checks each wordline's accumulated disturbance against a threshold, relocates the valid pages of any heavily-disturbed wordline, and erases the block once nothing valid remains.

evidence: Fig. 7 shows how STRAWFTL manages read-disturbance at a WL-granularity.
STRAWFTL copies the valid pages to free pages before the next interval, thereby preventing read-disturbance-induced data corruption.
If the block contains no valid pages after the checking procedure, STRAWFTL erases the block and resets all associated counters.

summary: This flowchart shows how STRAWFTL manages NAND flash read disturbance at wordline (WL) granularity. Every read request increments per-block and per-WL read counters (RC[BLK_tgt]++, RC[WL_tgt]++). When the block's counter reaches a predefined interval, STRAWFTL loops over every valid WL in the block and asks whether it is heavily-disturbed; if so, that WL's valid pages are copied to free pages before disturbance can corrupt them. Once all WLs have been checked, the flowchart asks whether the block is now empty of valid pages: if so, STRAWFTL erases the block and resets its counters before ending, and if not, it simply ends until the next interval. Colour groups the four stages (orange counting, blue per-WL checking and copying, green erasing) so the procedure's shape is visible at a glance.
summary_zh: 该流程图示STRAWFTL按WL粒度管理读干扰：每次读请求递增块与WL读计数；每隔一定间隔遍历块内所有有效WL，若某WL被严重干扰则将其有效页迁移到空闲页；检查完后若块已空则擦除该块并重置计数器，否则结束。
